summary: The article argues that long-term investors can accumulate Reliance Industries (RIL) on dips despite its roughly 11% three-year CAGR trailing the Nifty 50's little over 14%. It cites reasonable valuations, leadership in digital (Jio) and retail, a stable O2C business, and a green energy push that the market has not yet priced in. A sum-of-the-parts valuation puts enterprise value around $214 billion, roughly matching the current market cap after debt, leaving upside from E&P and green energy.
one_line: Business Line argues Reliance Industries, despite lagging the Nifty 50 over three years, is worth accumulating on dips given Jio, retail, O2C and unpriced green energy.
key_facts: RIL stock underperformed from 2007 to 2017 but has trebled over the last six years.
On a three-year basis RIL delivered 11 per cent CAGR (including demerged Jio Financial Services value) versus a little over 14 per cent for Nifty 50.
RIL tends to underperform when in a heavy investment phase, as it is now with green energy ventures.
Reliance Retail grew from 1,691 stores in FY14 to 18,040 stores (over 66 million sq ft) by FY23, with only about 3 per cent market share; Walmart holds a little over 10 per cent of US retail.
Reliance Retail's FY21-23 revenue and EBITDA CAGR were 38 and 50 per cent respectively, aided by acquisitions totalling $1.2 billion such as Netmeds, Zivame, Clovia and Urban Ladder.

O2C and E&P still account for 45-50 per cent of RIL's consolidated EBITDA; O2C is valued at about $75 billion, unchanged from the 2019 Saudi Aramco stake-sale talks, and E&P is under 10 per cent of RIL value.
RIL has committed ₹75,000 crore to green energy: ₹60,000 crore for a green energy complex on 5,000 acres at Jamnagar and ₹15,000 crore for partnerships, future technologies and value chain.
RIL trades at 24 times trailing twelve-month earnings, above its pre-Covid three-year average of around 20 times.
Reliance Retail Ventures is valued at about $100 billion (₹8.3 lakh crore) and RIL owns 83 per cent of it.
Reliance Jio was valued at $63 billion in 2020 and is now valued at $80-90 billion (10 to 11x one-year forward EBITDA); RIL holds 67 per cent.

SOTP gives an enterprise value of about $214 billion; with net debt of around $15 billion, valuation is about $200 billion, matching the current market cap, with zero value given to green energy, E&P, media and real estate.
Jio is the largest telecom services company in a largely duopolistic market with Bharti Airtel, given survival issues at Vodafone Idea; 5G is expected to drive higher ARPUs.
